_comment: The ONE table of cases for the poster theme library, read by BOTH implementations:
server/src/modules/posters/theme-library.spec.ts and
composeApp/src/androidUnitTest/.../PosterThemesTest.kt.
The rule exists twice, in two languages, because the SERVER refuses a theme that does
not belong to the occasion's family and the CLIENT filters the picker so the user never
sees one. Neither half can be dropped: a client that only filtered would let a tampered
request through, and a server that only validated would show somebody a cake on a
remembrance and then 400 when they tapped it. MILESTONE_CHECKLIST.md §C — a rule
implemented twice is held to one shared table of cases, and the table is this file,
not a copy of it.
== TBD-5 IS NOT ANSWERED, AND THESE ARE NOT ART DIRECTION ==
REQUIREMENTS.md §18 lists TBD-5 — 'visual identity: palette, type, icon, poster template
art direction' — as due at M4. It is still open. FR-POS-04 asks for themes that are
HAND-APPROVED and FR-POS-13 asks for a solemn family, and neither is a thing a session
can decide: 'hand-approved' names a hand.
So every theme below is a PLACEHOLDER and says so in its own display name. Their
`approved` flag is false in theme_cache until a person sets it, and the picker only ever
offers approved rows. What is being built and tested here is the MECHANISM — the
families, the filter, the cache key, the compositor's geometry. What the posters look
like is Dipen's, and when he answers TBD-5 the fix is this file and the palettes, not
the pipeline. docs/M6_PLAN.md §2.1.
== FR-POS-13, as a lexicon on the DATA rather than on a prompt ==
FR-POS-13: a solemn theme has a 'muted palette, no balloons, confetti, cake or party
motifs'. `banned_on_solemn` below is that sentence as a list, and both suites assert no
SOLEMN theme's id, display name, art prompt or motif list contains any of those words.
M5 §0.3 learned where a lexicon assertion can and cannot live: it CANNOT be pointed at a
prompt, because a prompt has to name what it forbids — 'never congratulate' fails its own
check. It CAN be pointed at the words a recipient actually reads, or at data like this.
These are motifs that get drawn, so this is the right surface for it.
== REQUIREMENTS.md §11 files this under CORRECTNESS ==
'Automated tests assert that no SOLEMN event can ever produce celebratory copy, a
celebratory template, a gift suggestion or a T-7 gifting reminder.' The middle clause is
M6's, and the `offered: false` rows in `picker_cases` are the test that must go RED if
somebody puts a celebratory theme back into the solemn family — docs/BUILD_PROMPT_M6.md,
definition of done item 2.
_family_for_sentiment: The mapping, in one place. It is one-to-one today and it is still written down rather
than inlined, because FR-POS-13's filter is the thing most likely to go wrong in this
milestone and a mapping nobody can point at is a mapping two call sites will disagree
about. A sentiment is a fact about an occasion; a family is a property of a picture.
_aspect_ratios: FR-POS-05's three output formats, as the aspect-ratio component of FR-POS-03's cache
key. STATUS is the default — the WhatsApp status size, which is what this product is

separate entries in a separate family, not celebratory themes with the motifs taken
out. domain/Tone.kt took the same decision for words and said why: a conditional is
a thing someone can forget, and a set you have to pick is a thing the compiler makes
you pick.
